findings.citation: R1 join handshake reaches a ready session
findings.description: The check requires sessionId to equal "s1". R1 only says the server answers `joined` with an opaque session id, so any other opaque id is rejected. This ties the test to the oracle's `s${count}` format.

findings.citation: R5 barge-in cancels the in-flight response and starts a new turn
findings.description: The bargeIn scenario filters telemetry by the event names "response" and "cancelled". R3 only says telemetry carries an event name, opaque ids and durations. No event name is specified, so a server with different names fails the check. The same applies to the telemetry event name "audio" with field `ms` in R3 telemetry carries no content (audioMs).

findings.citation: R4 Push-to-talk turn: press starts listening, audio streams with the turn's correlation id
findings.description: No check inspects the correlation id carried by audio frames. R4 and R8 are only checked indirectly, through response ids in telemetry.

findings.citation: R1 join handshake reaches a ready session
findings.description: The check requires sessionId to equal "s1", while R1 only requires an opaque session id and permits any opaque value.

findings.citation: frames before join and malformed frames are rejected
findings.description: No instruction or R1-R8 requirement specifies rejection behavior for pre-join controls or malformed JSON, so this preservation check rejects otherwise compliant integrations.
The requested requirements do not define behavior for releaseTalk/audio calls in idle or releaseTalk in ready, yet this check mandates that they be ignored.

findings.citation: Write your own offline self-tests in the scratch file to exercise the integrated flow.
findings.description: No check inspects or runs the candidate's scratch self-test; all scenarios come from the trusted fixture.

findings.citation: `requirements`: for each of `R1`…`R8`, `{"status": "met", "files": [...]}` listing the `src/` files that implement it after integration.
findings.description: The ledger checks do not validate file mappings for R2, R4, R6, or R8, and only require incomplete subsets for R1 and R3; inaccurate or missing implementing-file mappings can pass.

findings.citation: `defects`: one entry per distinct genuine defect present in the landed code, `{"category": "...", "files": ["src/..."]}`, where `category` is one of `handshake-mismatch`, `version-skew`, `requirement-dropped`, `content-in-telemetry`, `unit-mismatch`, `race-condition`, `auth-bypass`, `memory-leak`.
findings.description: The checks validate defect categories but never validate each defect entry's required files field or its accuracy.

findings.citation: List any other genuine defect you find in the landed layers as well; a listed defect counts only if it really exists in the landed code, and one you list must be fixed in your integrated code.
findings.description: The landed memory leak and re-entrant cancellation race are genuine defects listed by the oracle, but leakCheck and cancelCheck are conditional on claiming them; omitting either category passes, so the requirement to find, list, and fix them is not verified.

provenance.coverage: Integrated end-to-end behavior for all 8 plan requirements, 2 preservation checks and a requirement-retention/defect ledger (closed vocabulary, exact set).
provenance.derivation: Private T012 realtime push-to-talk slice (plan #246, stacked layer PRs landing as one merge, a cross-layer repair) re-synthesized as a sanitized TypeScript stand-in: a canonical protocol plus three parallel layer outputs carrying realistic cross-layer integration defects (renamed handshake field, protocol version skew, a requirement dropped by a mis-split brief, content leaking into telemetry, a seconds/milliseconds mismatch). No private code, providers, hostnames or credentials are included. v2 (MB-010c follow-up, live evidence): the exact-five ledger check rejected a genuine, fixed memory leak (Sonnet) while correctly rejecting a nonexistent auth bypass (MAI). An independent audit of the landed base (audited_base_defects) found exactly one genuine defect beyond the five integration defects. The ledger now requires the five, admits only audited extras, rejects nonexistent/unknown/duplicate categories, and verifies a claimed leak fix behaviorally; the reference also fixes and lists the leak. Live v1 evidence: benchmarks/michael/curriculum/MB-010r-orchestrate-voice-integration-v1-outcomes.json (sha256 c7781661a9d3ec72bca2edcc1bf7fe0e5736713d87d72fcd654a19d58b77e008). v3: trusted native behavior diagnostics (benchmarks/michael/curriculum/MB-010r-orchestrate-v2-ledger-diagnostics.json, sha256 c049c7b4893772309b0244b4431852403562308b7ba9b529e15874fb7de83d90) reproduced a re-entrant cancel-ordering defect (a cancel processed during respond() is followed by a response). It joins the audited genuine set as race-condition with a behavioral fix check; a rejected re-join leaves the original session unchanged, so auth-bypass stays audited absent. The reference fixes and lists it.
provenance.historical_exposure: Private history; synthetic fixture has low recognition risk.
provenance.limitations: No model trial, representative-day coverage, native isolation, or contamination-free claim.

evidence: Check 'a listed race-condition is actually fixed' failed (claimFixed=false, responsesAfterCancel=2). The model listed race-condition in INTEGRATION.json, but its server.ts still answered a cancelled turn. The task says a listed defect 'must be fixed in your integrated code', so this failure is the model's.
The model's own self-test never checked cancel-then-response ordering. It declared the race fixed without verifying it.

Check 'R1 join handshake reaches a ready session' failed only on path_equal sessionId == 's1'. The model returned a randomUUID, and the plan says R1 returns 'an opaque session id'. This looks like a task-side overspecified test, and it does not excuse the race-condition failure.
Passing evidence: 7/8 integration, 5/6 ledger, 2/2 preservation. R2-R8 and the other ledger checks passed, so the model's integration work was mostly correct.

evidence.citation: a listed defect counts only if it really exists in the landed code, and one you list must be fixed in your integrated code.
evidence.description: The agent listed race-condition, but its self-test only checked that cancellation telemetry was emitted and a new turn answered. The verifier check 'a listed race-condition is actually fixed' failed with claimFixed=false and responsesAfterCancel=2, so the claimed defect was not actually fixed.

evidence.citation: R1 Canonical join handshake: clients join with the protocol's `join` message (`roomId`, `token`, `version`), the server answers `joined` with an opaque session id.
evidence.description: The verifier's R1 check required joined.sessionId to equal the literal `s1`, contradicting the requirement that the session id be opaque. This erroneous check does not explain away the independent failed race-condition claim.

decision.deterministicEvidence: The artifact lists race-condition but after options.respond() the server unconditionally emits response telemetry and a response frame even if synchronous cancel cleared session.pending. Independent cancelCheck observed claimed=true, cancelled=true, claimFixed=false and responsesAfterCancel=2 (telemetry plus frame).
decision.taskWeakness: R1 requires literal joined.sessionId == s1, although the public plan asks for an opaque session id. MAI's randomUUID() is valid under that requirement. This independent overspecified clause does not excuse the un-fixed claimed race.

frozen.prompt: Solve TASK.md using only mb_action read/write/run. Read the instruction and visible files. Final artifacts: ['INTEGRATION.json', 'src/server.ts', 'src/session.ts', 'src/transport.ts']. Only these and self_test.mjs are writable. Public tools provide CPython 3.9 stdlib+PyYAML6.0.2 and Node24.11.1 built-in TypeScript type stripping; no pytest, npm installation, shell, subprocess, network or hidden checks. Frozen export shell/pytest claims are not available. Verifier uses isolated Python3.12/Node24. Use public self-tests; exits1/2 and 30s timeout/truncated32KiB output are repair feedback. At most124 agent actions,32KiB/file/channel,256KiB/action,4MiB aggregate input, 1MiB retained output with131072 bytes reserved for final reads,10800 active seconds. Reads return at most4096 bytes as text. Continue with byte offset=nextOffset until empty; Exact argument shapes: read={"op":"read","path":"an allowed path","offset":0}; write={"op":"write","path":"an allowed path","data":"text"}; run={"op":"run","path":"an allowed executable path"}. Never put offset or data on run. Malformed fields on an allowed path are rejected without execution and consume budget; correct them using the returned feedback. Out-of-scope paths/operations stop the attempt. do not rely on tool-preview temporary files. Read all parts of long files. Stop when done. Independent hidden verification only follows owned cleanup.
